svg.aria-label: Diagram: why Packet Mirroring answers the sampling problem by capturing every packet including payloads and headers, and what that costs, since mirroring happens on the virtual machine rather than on the network and therefore triples egress bandwidth on a mirrored instance; why the mirrored copy is plaintext because VPC encryption happens in the hypervisor and the mirror is taken before it; the ordering model where policy priority is fixed at 1000 and specificity decides instead, unlike every firewall rule in this block; and the migration trap where creating a single Network Security Integration mirroring rule makes the data plane disregard every VPC Packet Mirroring configuration for every workload
svg.title: Packet Mirroring: every packet, taken on the VM, in plaintext, with an ordering model that is not priority
svg.text: This is the instrument that does not sample. The price is paid on the VM, not by Google.
And Google now recommends a different product for new deployments, which is its own trap.
What it gives you, after three posts of estimates
It CLONES the traffic of specified instances and forwards it for examination, capturing ALL
traffic and packet data, INCLUDING PAYLOADS AND HEADERS.
It exports all traffic, NOT only the traffic between sampling periods — the direct answer
to #77, where a primary sampling rate you cannot set decided what you ever saw.
Sources are chosen by subnet, network tag or instance name. A subnet includes FUTURE VMs.
Where the mirror is taken, and what that costs you
The mirroring happens ON THE VM INSTANCES, NOT ON THE NETWORK. So it consumes the
mirrored instance’s own bandwidth.
Google’s worked example: 1 Gbps in and 1 Gbps out becomes 1 Gbps ingress and 3 GBPS
EGRESS — 1 normal plus 2 mirrored. Egress triples.
#77 said flow logs add no delay or performance penalty. This is the opposite trade.
The consequence nobody expects: the copy is in the clear
Mirrored traffic is encrypted ONLY IF THE VM ENCRYPTS IT AT THE APPLICATION LAYER.
VM-to-VM traffic inside and across peered VPCs IS encrypted — but the encryption happens
IN THE HYPERVISORS, and from the VM’s perspective the traffic is not encrypted.
The mirror is taken before that layer. Full plaintext payloads ship to the collector fleet.
The one place in this block where specificity decides, not priority
Policy priority is ALWAYS 1000 AND CANNOT BE CHANGED. There is nothing to tune.
Overlapping policies resolve by MOST SPECIFIC CIDR RANGE, then most specific protocol —
exactly the longest-prefix logic #70 said firewall rules never use.
Two IDENTICAL policies are not supported, and Google may pick a DIFFERENT ONE each time
the traffic is re-evaluated. Non-deterministic, by documentation.
The migration trap in the product Google tells you to use instead
Network Security Integration mirroring puts the rules in the GLOBAL NETWORK FIREWALL POLICY
from #74, adds Geneve encapsulation and a DO_NOT_MIRROR action. Regional policies cannot.
BUT it takes PRECEDENCE: create one NSI mirroring rule, even implicitly, and the data plane
DISREGARDS ALL VPC Packet Mirroring configurations FOR ALL WORKLOADS.
Mirror HTTP the new way and your old ICMP capture stops. Google states this outright.
COST: $0.008 per gibibyte of data processed, no per-VM charge and no charge for the
forwarding rules — roughly 62 times cheaper per gibibyte than #76 and #77’s vended logs.
The rate is tiny; the gibibytes are not sampled. The collector fleet is yours to pay for.
